rules.category: Every prompt has one category. A slash command is a setting (/model, /effort, /fast, /config, /permissions, /output-style), a session command (/clear, /resume, /compact, /remote-control, /continue, /rename; /rc is short for /remote-control and the typo /moidel counts as /model) or another command (any other slash command), except that /btw or /goal followed by text is an instruction (the text is the prompt). Text starting with ! is a shell command (Claude Code runs it in the shell). Of the rest, a prompt that only answers a choice or acknowledges is a decision, and everything else is an instruction.
rules.decision: After lowercasing and replacing punctuation with spaces, the prompt is a single choice letter (a-d) or number (one or two digits, answering a numbered choice), or 1-3 words all drawn from {a, agreed, ahead, approve, approved, b, c, continue, d, go, lgtm, no, ok, proceed, sure, y, yes}. Slash commands are never decisions.
rules.articleWork: A session is article work if it has a prompt on or after 2026-10-08 00:00 Pacific AND (any of its prompts was typed in a project path containing 'ghostty-website', OR any of its prompts matches \b(article|journey|website|porting page|disclosure)\b, case-insensitive). Only that session's prompts on or after the cutoff are tagged; earlier prompts never are. The author corrected 3 sessions by hand: 2 untagged, 1 tagged.
rules.commits: A prompt's window runs from the prompt to the next human prompt of the same session (for the session's last prompt: to the session's last recorded activity, or 12 h when unknown), capped at 12 h and never past the extraction cutoff. Commits authored in the window are linked as follows. A commit is never linked when its Claude-Session trailer, or the `[branch sha]` git output in a surviving transcript, ties it to other human sessions only. session-window: the session's git branch is known (transcript, rustty-stats or Codex metadata) and the commit either shows up in this session's own transcripts (main, subagent or workflow files) or landed on that branch (made on it, merged into it through a chain of merges, or reachable from its current tip). time-window-branch: the branch is unknown and every commit in the window carries the same branch label. none: otherwise. Branch labels come from the `[branch sha]` lines git prints on commit (surviving transcripts), else from the oldest merge that brought the commit in, else from the local branch that reaches it. After linking, a commit linked from prompts of two or more human sessions keeps only the links backed by evidence: the commit's `[branch sha]` git output appears in that session's own transcripts, or its Claude-Session trailer names a cloud session bridged from that session. Other links to it are removed; a prompt left with no commits gets basis `ambiguous`.
rules.sessions: A session is one Claude Code or Codex session id on one machine. It spans the Pacific days from its first to its last human prompt (a resumed session keeps its id, so its span includes the days between). A session counts as open on a Pacific day when it has at least one prompt that day that is an instruction or a decision (not a slash command or a shell command). A session whose every prompt is a slash command or a shell command is a command-only session.
